answer: Cryptographic sortition elects agents by staking identity to unpredictable beacon randomness. Each agent signs its commitment with a digital quill tied to the current beacon output. A lagoon of low-stake sybils cannot concentrate probability because weights are quadratic and identities must pre-commit before the reveal. Nodes verify sortition proofs independently, rejecting scores outside the elected quorum. Large-scale sybil farming becomes statistically infeasible without prior capital.
